title: cymbopogon proximus var. sennarensis
intro: Cymbopogon proximus var. sennarensis, commonly known as East African lemongrass, is a type of perennial grass found in the tropical regions of East Africa. This plant has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antifungal properties, making it effective in treating various health issues such as digestive problems, fever, and respiratory infections. The therapeutic actions of East African lemongrass include analgesic, antipyretic, and expectorant properties, which contribute to its use in traditional medicine. The bioactive constituents of this plant include essential oils such as citral, geraniol, and limonene, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and contribute to its use in aromatherapy and traditional medicine practices.
